title: Recruitment & selection
examples: What is the difference between recruiting and selecting staff?
When should a company use external recruitment?
Can you explain the steps in the hiring process?

explain.say: Today we will learn about how businesses find and choose staff.

items: Selection means choosing the best one.

explain.say: Internal recruitment uses people already working at the company.
External recruitment looks for people outside the company.
The selection process involves several steps to choose staff.
For example, a local bakery might advertise a baker job.
In real life, when you apply for a part-time job, you are going through selection.

faq.q: What is the main difference between internal and external recruitment?
faq.a: Internal recruitment uses existing employees, which can boost morale. External recruitment brings in new ideas from outside the company.
asks: Should a company promote or hire from outside?
What are the pros and cons of using current staff?

faq.q: What is a job description in the selection process?
faq.a: It is a written document that lists the duties and responsibilities of the job. It tells people what the job actually involves.
asks: What do I need to write for a job description?
Is a job description the same as a job specification?

faq.q: Why might a company prefer external recruitment?
faq.a: They might want new skills or a fresh perspective that current staff do not have. This helps the business grow in new ways.
asks: When is it better to hire from outside?
What if we need totally new skills?

faq.q: Does the selection process always involve an interview?
faq.a: While interviews are common, the process might also include tests or practical assessments. It depends on the type of job.
asks: Do I always have to do an interview?
What else can happen after I apply?

faq.q: Is promotion always better than hiring someone new?
faq.a: It can be, as it rewards loyalty and keeps staff happy. However, new people might bring necessary changes.
asks: Is promotion always the best choice?
What if the current staff is too comfortable?

facts: Internal recruitment can boost staff morale and loyalty.
External recruitment can bring in new ideas and skills.
The selection process usually moves from advertising to interviewing.
A job description details the tasks of the role.

quiz.say: A manager decides to move a skilled worker to a different department within the same company. This is an example of:
quiz.why: Transfer means moving an employee to a different role inside the business.

wrong.0: Promotion means moving to a higher level or more responsibility.
wrong.1: External recruitment means hiring someone who does not currently work there.
wrong.2: Selection is the overall process of choosing staff, not the movement itself.

quiz.say: A company posts an advertisement on a national job website to find a new accountant. This method is:
quiz.why: Posting online means looking outside the company for candidates.

wrong.0: Internal recruitment uses people already employed by the business.
wrong.1: A job specification lists the skills needed, not the method of finding people.
wrong.3: Promotion only involves current employees moving up.

quiz.say: Which step immediately follows receiving applications in the selection process?
quiz.why: After you get applications, the next logical step is to talk to the candidates.

wrong.0: A careers fair is a source of recruitment, not a step in the selection process itself.
wrong.2: This happens at the very beginning, before any applications are received.
wrong.3: The offer is the final step, happening after the interviews are complete.
